answers.how: Measured the horizontal body length (beak-to-tail extent) of the small bird across frames 0 to 8 as 106.6 px (55.5/1000 of image width) and the big bird across frames 0 to 4 as 174.7 px (91.0/1000 of image width). Using the prior length of the small bird = 0.94 m, the length of the big bird is 0.94 * (91.0 / 55.5) = 1.54 m.

Using the scale from the small bird's length (0.94 m / 106.6 px = 0.00882 m/px in 1920x1080), measured the vertical wingspan extent of the big bird from its initial pose in frame 0 (225.8 px, 1.99 m) to its full flat wingspan in frame 4 (335.9 px, 2.96 m), giving a representative width of 2.48 m.

Using the scale 0.00882 m/px from the small bird's body length (106.6 px = 0.94 m), measured the vertical wingspan extent of the small bird from frame 0 (167.4 px, 1.48 m) to its full flat wingspan in frames 2 and 4 (195.5 px, 1.72 m), giving a width of 1.60 m.

Tracked the horizontal center of the small bird across frames 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 (1178.4 px, 1269.6 px, 1453.9 px, 1638.2 px, 1822.6 px in 1920x1080). The bird moves at a steady rate of 92.16 px/frame (2211.8 px/s at 24 fps). Converting with 0.00882 m/px gives an average speed of ~19.4 m/s.

Tracked the horizontal position of the big bird across frames 0, 2, 4, and 6 (tail tip at 787.2 px, 636.5 px, 336.0 px, and 35.5 px in 1920x1080). The big bird moves left at a constant rate of 150.24 px/frame (3605.8 px/s at 24 fps). Converting with 0.00882 m/px gives an average speed of ~31.5 m/s.

Both birds fly along the same horizontal centerline (y = 555 px) in opposite directions. At t = 0 s, their centers are separated by 478.6 px (4.22 m), and their separation increases at a constant rate of 242.4 px/frame (2.138 m/frame, or 51.32 m/s). Extrapolating to t = 0.5 s (frame 12) gives a horizontal distance of 28.8 m.
